paper: NBER Working Paper 35301, Do Voters Punish Inflation or Pay Cuts? Inflation and Real Wages in U.S. Elections
nber_pdf_status: HTTP 403 Cloudflare/access page in the current environment
paper_version: May 28, 2026 version shown in the acquired author PDF

design.county_period: 2020 and 2024 presidential elections; 2021 to 2024 local cost and wage changes
design.price_source: Economic Policy Institute Family Budget Calculator, seven categories; county cost-of-living measure rather than a fixed CPI basket
design.wage_source: BLS Quarterly Census of Employment and Wages covered wages and average pay
design.election_source: MIT Election Data and Science Lab county returns
design.controls: Census/ACS, USDA, and BEA socioeconomic controls; urbanization, density, age, education, real GDP, and demographic composition
design.inference: heteroskedasticity-robust standard errors and 100-replication state-cluster block bootstrap standard errors

district_check.competitive_definition: absolute two-party Republican margin below 10 percentage points in the 2020 House race
district_check.boundary: competitive-district estimates are small and imprecise; district aggregation adds measurement error

audit_notes: The paper explicitly states that county-level results cannot identify individual voter behavior and may reflect compositional changes in the electorate.
The EPI Family Budget Calculator is a cost-of-living measure for a defined family structure, not a direct household expenditure panel.
The preferred regression is descriptive conditional on state effects and controls; the paper discusses the need for additional design elements to identify shocks.
The author PDF was acquired for method/table audit; no paper replication code or county microdata were added to the repository.
